(This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Mississippi does NOT conform to federal tax treaties and re-taxes treaty-exempt income. Two .gov findings establish this. (1) The MS DOR Individual Income Tax FAQ states: "Does Mississippi honor federal income tax exemption treaties between the United States and other foreign countries? No, as a general rule, Mississippi does not follow federal income tax exemption treaties. Any income earned on a 1042S should be reported on the Mississippi return as taxable income." (2) Unlike most states, MS does NOT start from federal AGI — the 2025 Form 80-105 builds Mississippi income from scratch line-by-line (wages through other income; "Total income" line 49) and then applies MS-specific adjustments to reach "Mississippi adjusted gross income" (line 66). Because the return is built from gross income items rather than inheriting the federal AGI exclusion, treaty-exempt wages/income (e.g., reported on a 1042-S) are pulled into Mississippi taxable income directly; no special add-back schedule is needed. Net effect: treaty-exempt income IS taxed by Mississippi, so conforms_to_federal_treaties = false.

Pack notes: 2025 RATE CUT (HB 531 phase-in): the rate on taxable income in excess of $10,000 DROPS to 4.4% (2024: 4.7%); the 0% band on the first $10,000 is unchanged. This is the ONLY change from 2024 - exemptions and standard deductions are identical. The 2025 Build Up Mississippi Act (HB 1, eff. 7/1/2025) keeps 2025 at 4.4% and 2026 at 4.0% and adds later cuts (2027 3.75%, 2028 3.5%, 2029 3.25%, 2030+ 3%, contingent reductions below 3% from 2031) - do NOT use those for 2025. Base guidance: Supply Mississippi adjusted gross income: 2025 Form 80-105 (resident return), page 1, line 13 (from page 2, line 66 'Mississippi adjusted gross income'). Mississippi does NOT start from federal AGI - the return builds MS income from its own line items minus MS adjustments. Do NOT supply federal AGI. The pack ships the subtractions to get from line 13 to line 16 'Mississippi taxable income' for a standard-deduction filer: the shipped standard_deduction per status is the SUM of the MS standard deduction and the MS filing-status exemption, and the shipped dependent exemption is $1,500 each; the rate schedule then reproduces line 17. Itemizers (Form 80-108 Schedule A) and nonresident/part-year filers (Form 80-205) must be computed on the form instead. Adjudication note (two-pass): exemptions_count must be 0 - the Mississippi per-status personal exemption ($6,000 single/MFS, $12,000 MFJ, $8,000 Head of Family) is FOLDED INTO the shipped standard_deduction amounts, never applied per count. Only dependents_count is applied ($1,500 each). 2025 Mississippi rates (instructions p.22, 'TAX RATES'): 0% on the first $10,000.00 of taxable income and 4.4% on taxable income in excess of $10,000.00. ONE schedule covers ALL filing statuses (the Schedule of Tax Computation has no per-status rate columns); it is duplicated per status here. MODELING NOTE - shipped standard_deduction is a COMBINED per-status amount: Mississippi's personal exemption is a fixed per-FILING-STATUS amount (Single $6,000; MFJ/Combined $12,000; MFS $6,000 per spouse; Head of Family $8,000), not a per-person amount. The shipped standard_deduction = MS standard deduction + MS filing-status exemption: Single $2,300 + $6,000 = $8,300; MFJ $4,600 + $12,000 = $16,600; MFS $2,300 + $6,000 = $8,300; Head of Family $3,400 + $8,000 = $11,400. No 'personal' exemption key is shipped, so exemptions_count has no effect. Corroboration: the booklet's own filing thresholds are exactly these sums ('Single... in excess of $8,300...; Married... in excess of $16,600...'). All amounts unchanged from 2024. MARRIED COMBINED RETURN (two-column) math is NOT modeled - can OVERSTATE tax by up to $440 for two-income couples in 2025: on a combined return where both spouses have positive taxable income (Form 80-105 columns A and B), the Schedule of Tax Computation line 1 gives EACH column its own first $10,000 at 0%, so up to $20,000 is taxed at 0% (the DOR FAQ confirms: 'If married filing joint, the first $10,000 of each taxpayer's taxable income is exempt'). This pack's single-base married_filing_jointly computation gives only one $10,000 zero band and matches the form only when all income is in Column A (one-income couple). MARRIED FILING SEPARATELY: Form 80-105 line 15 instruction halves the total authorized exemptions (($12,000 + $1,500 x dependents)/2 = $6,000 + $750 per dependent), and any unused portion of one spouse's standard deduction or exemption may NOT be used by the other spouse. The shipped $8,300 is exact for MFS with zero dependents; with dependents the shipped $1,500/dependent overstates the exemption by $750 each - compute on the form. Head of Family (Mississippi's head-of-household status) REQUIRES at least one dependent living in the home the entire year; that required dependent IS counted and DOES receive the $1,500 dependent exemption - pass it in dependents_count. Qualifying surviving spouse mapping: Mississippi's 'Married - Spouse Died in Tax Year (2025)' status uses the identical $12,000 exemption and $4,600 standard deduction as Married Filing Joint/Combined, so it maps cleanly to married_filing_jointly. Mississippi has no multi-year qualifying-surviving-spouse status. Age 65-or-over and blind additional exemptions ($1,500 per box checked, taxpayer and spouse only, Form 80-105 line 8) are base reductions but are NOT applied by calc.state_tax - take them on the form (shipped as informational 'age_65'/'blind' keys only). Itemized deductions: filers may itemize on Form 80-108 Schedule A instead of the standard deduction (state income taxes and MS gaming losses are NOT deductible); this pack assumes the standard deduction. Tax CREDITS are not modeled: line 18 credit for income tax paid to another state (Form 80-160) and line 19 other credits (Form 80-401 - e.g. Dependent Care Credit 2025 code 44 = 25% of the federal credit for federal AGI <= $50,000; Child Adoption Credit code 25) are subtracted from line 17 tax AFTER the rate schedule; they are credits, not exemptions. No tax-table mandate: Mississippi has no lookup-table requirement - every filer computes line 17 with the Schedule of Tax Computation bracket math, so the pack's marginal math matches the form exactly. The schedule prints no additive constants, so there is no rounded-constant divergence to quantify. Rounding: the booklet mandates whole-dollar rounding (round down amounts under $.50, round up amounts of $.50 and over) - identical to the engine's round-half-up. Nonresidents and part-year residents file Form 80-205 (taxable income line 19, tax line 20) and must PRORATE deductions and exemptions by the MS-income ratio - this pack models only the full-year resident Form 80-105.
